purpose: Define how organs consume infrastructure capabilities without hardcoded physical assumptions or cortex-local execution shortcuts.
principles: Organs consume named capabilities, not accidental hosts, paths, or local binaries.
Registry desired state names roles and services; runtime evidence proves whether they are alive.
Cortex sessions dispatch lifecycle intent; physical execution belongs to declared organs.
Provider, storage, mesh, fleet, and lifecycle mutations must cross a port or MCP/kernel contract.

native_lifecycle.mcp_reload: cynic_lifecycle_dispatch(profile="mcp-reload") or make mcp-reload-request as MCP-unavailable operator transport
native_lifecycle.gate_2: cynic_lifecycle_dispatch(profile="gate-2") or make gate-2-request as MCP-unavailable operator transport
native_lifecycle.deploy: cynic_lifecycle_dispatch(profile="deploy") or make deploy-request as MCP-unavailable operator transport

forbidden_patterns.detail: MCP builds must be lifecycle-dispatched to the registry build runner.
MCP binaries must be installed by the registry lifecycle executor, not from a cortex-local release artifact.
Kernel release artifacts must move through lifecycle dispatch, not a cortex-local copy.
Primary dependency updates must use declared native update commands, not ad-hoc curl-pipe-shell.
Organs and wrappers must resolve operator paths from environment, registry, passwd, or runtime evidence.
SurrealDB must be consumed through storage_primary/Synapse or the Kernel coordination API, not a cortex-local localhost endpoint.
